title: Localization embeds into generic fibre localizations
statement: Let $R\to B$ be a flat homomorphism of commutative rings of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra]. Suppose $B\otimes_R K$ is a domain for every prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and field extension $K/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Let $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}$ be the inverse image of the zero prime of $B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. With spectra and localization as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-module-localization], the natural map $$B\longrightarrow\prod_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R}B_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}$$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0810, final paragraph, generic-fibre localization injection; using Tag 05DH, lemma-base-change-universally-flat, after localization of the base.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-geometrically-integral-projective] to $R\to B$. Its flatness and finite-presentation hypotheses are the stated hypotheses on $R\to B$, and its geometric-integrality hypothesis is exactly the stated domain condition for every extension of each residue field. Thus $B$ is a projective $R$-module.

For each $\mathfrak p$, apply [lem-trf-fibre-generic-localization-residue-flat] with $F=B\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, a nonzero domain by the hypothesis with $K=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. The prime it constructs is $\ker(B\to F)$, exactly $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}$ since the inverse image of the zero ideal is the kernel. It contracts to $\mathfrak p$ and supplies the canonical map $u_{\mathfrak p}:(R\setminus\mathfrak p)^{-1}B\to D_{\mathfrak p}=B_{\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}}$. The lemma gives flatness of $D_{\mathfrak p}$ over $R_{\mathfrak p}$. Its final clause asserts injectivity of the actual reduction of $u_{\mathfrak p}$ modulo $\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$, using the stated quotient-to-localized-fibre comparison.

source.place: Tag 0810, lemma-helper-blowup-affine-space, final paragraph: fibre-generic localization preparation.

proof.text: Use [lem-trf-projective-local-flat-family-injectivity] with $M=B$, $N_{\mathfrak p}=D_{\mathfrak p}$ and $v_{\mathfrak p}:B\to D_{\mathfrak p}$ the localization homomorphism. Restrict scalars along $R\to R_{\mathfrak p}$; this makes $v_{\mathfrak p}$ $R$-linear because $v_{\mathfrak p}(rb)=v_{\mathfrak p}(r)v_{\mathfrak p}(b)$. Step 1 gives projectivity of $M$. The canonical $R_{\mathfrak p}$-algebra structure from step 2 gives the required local module structure on $N_{\mathfrak p}$ and its flatness. The induced map $M_{\mathfrak p}\to N_{\mathfrak p}$ is exactly $u_{\mathfrak p}$: both send $b/s$ to $s^{-1}v_{\mathfrak p}(b)=b/s$. The denominator is invertible since $\mathfrak q_{\mathfrak p}$ contracts to $\mathfrak p$. Hence step 2 also gives injectivity of its reduction. The family lemma now gives injectivity of $b\mapsto(v_{\mathfrak p}(b))_{\mathfrak p}$, the underlying function of the displayed ring homomorphism. This proves the stated injectivity, including $R=0$, where a unital $R$-algebra $B$ is zero and the product is empty.
